thread:
maya: sharing a draft for a normalized benchmark protocol to compare replay vs synthetic for continuous batching + kernel selection. want feedback on assumptions and edge cases.

maya: TL;DR: run pairs of runs (replay, synth) on the same infra snapshot, with KV-cache warmup stage, same seed traffic distribution, and a short steady-state window for apples-like comparisons. capture per-token p50/p95 latency, batch-size distribution, kernel switches, and kv-hit-rate over time.

liam: looks good. what do you mean by 'infra snapshot'? machine image + runtime flags?

maya: yes. same AMI/container image + same runtime args. we also pin the model variant (fp16 vs int8) and disable autoscaling. isolated node pool recommended.

raj: important: replay harness needs to preserve inter-arrival times and tenant mix. if replay compresses time we get different batching behavior.

maya: agreed — the replay tool will support two modes: wallclock and sped-up with preserved ordering but annotated real timestamps so we can reconstruct batching windows. default for this protocol is wallclock.

ben: can you paste the example harness config?

maya: 
```
# normalized-benchmark.yaml
mode: replay
traffic: tenant-mix-4.json
duration: 30m
warmup: 10m   # KV-cache & prefix warmup
steady_window: 10m
snapshot_image: rwinf/runner:v2026-03-01
runtime_flags:
  batch.max_delay_ms: 12
  batch.size_cap: 64
  kernel_selection: auto
  kv.prefetch: true
collect:
  - per_token_latency
  - batch_histogram
  - kernel_events
  - kv_hit_rate
```

maya: For synth we use the same tenant-mix profile but generate Poisson arrivals that match observed per-tenant IAT distributions. we do one-to-one mapping of session length and prompt length distribution.

sophia: How are we normalizing for KV cache warmup? 10m seems arbitrary.

maya: we do a 10m warmup, then reset metrics and start the steady window. warmup length configurable; we also run an explicit cold-run where cache is flushed to measure cold tail.

liam: About kernel selection: we should capture per-request chosen kernel id and model seq_len, then check for kernel flip-flops during a steady window. earlier regressions happened when kernel heuristics mis-evaluated short vs long tokens.

maya: exactly. collect kernel_events with fields: timestamp, kernel_id, seq_len, reason (latency_est/cost_est). we store them + traces for top 1% slow requests.

raj: fairness check: run multi-tenant with 4 tenants and introduce a high qps tenant at minute 15. measure how batch caps and max_delay affect smaller tenants' p95. propose this experiment grid: batch.size_cap in [32,64,128], batch.max_delay_ms in [6,12,24].

maya: added to the plan. we'll run the full grid for both replay & synth. total runs per grid cell: 3 seeds to capture noise.

ben: what's the regression detection criteria? last time we had a noisy p95.

maya: primary signals: steady-window p95 increase >5% or token-cost increase >3% for same throughput. secondary: increase in kernel_switch events >20% or kv_hit_rate drop >3pp. we alert on any primary signal.

infra-bot: deploybot: started run 1895-2345 on pool rutile-az1 (isolated). logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/1895-2345

liam: small nit: for synth mode, seed RNG and traffic variability should be recorded (seed, RNG version). add that to collect.

maya: done. also plan to attach a tiny post-run analysis notebook that produces a 1-page comparison: latency curves, batch histograms, kv-hit over time, kernel-flip timeline, and fairness heatmap.

raj: do we want to toggle kernel_selection: auto vs force-old to measure sensitivity?

maya: yes — we'll add a kernel-ablation axis: auto, prefer-old, prefer-new.

sophia: can we add a lightweight trace of queue occupancy per queue (tenant)? helps explain batching-induced latency.

maya: good call. adding queue_occupancy_sample every 100ms.

ben: any plan for storing raw data? these replays are large.

maya: raw traces go to s3://rwinf-bench/1895-2345/raw.tar.gz. processed metrics and notebook in s3://rwinf-bench/1895-2345/report.html. retention 30d by default.

liam: timeline?

maya: aiming to run the full grid tomorrow morning (UTC) and have initial report by EOD. please ping if you want a specific run.

raj: if this goes well we should add the protocol to the regression CI gating for runtime changes.

maya: agreed — next step: run, check for >5% p95 regressions, and if any, open a perf-regression issue with kernel and kv artifacts attached.

sophia: acked. I'll watch the runs.

ben: thanks maya — this protocol should help us finally compare replay vs synth reproducibly. :rocket:
